intro_html: Chile colorado is beef stewed in pure red chile sauce. No beans, no tomato base, no shortcuts through a can of enchilada sauce. Dried guajillos and anchos get soaked and blended, the chuck browns in flour first so the sauce clings, and then it just simmers until the beef gives up. Each bowl carries 36 grams of protein and 570 calories for about $6.08 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $6.08 a bowl (at everyday cost). Nine ingredients, and once you own the bag of dried chiles the recurring cost is basically beef, broth, and rice.
shop_smart: Buy dried chiles by the bag in the Latin foods aisle rather than in spice jars. The price difference per ounce is not small, it is enormous.
Chuck roast is the correct cut for a two hour braise. Anything more tender would cost more and fall apart into strings.
The flour dredge is a free thickener. It gives you a browned crust and a sauce that coats instead of running, from an ingredient you already own.
Rice cooked plain is the right base. The chile sauce is doing enough, and seasoning the rice would just muddy it.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Stem and seed the guajillo and ancho chiles along with the arbol chiles from the pantry list, and toast them briefly in a dry pan until fragrant.
Soak the toasted chiles in hot water for 20 minutes, then blend them with the onion, garlic, oregano, cumin, and a cup of the soaking liquid until smooth. Strain the sauce.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes, season with salt and black pepper, and toss them in the flour.
Brown the floured beef in the olive oil in batches in a heavy pot, working in batches so the flour crisps rather than steams.
Return all the beef, pour in the strained chile sauce and the beef broth, and add the bay leaves.
Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is fork tender and the sauce has darkened and thickened.
Pull the bay leaves, taste for salt, and cook the rice separately.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon that weight of beef and red chile sauce into each container, then add the same weight of rice to every one. Each bowl lands at 570 calories with 36 grams of protein.

head.description: Chile colorado meal prep: chuck roast dredged in flour and braised in a pure guajillo and ancho red chile sauce, served over rice. 570 calories, 36g protein, about $6.08 per serving (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: chile colorado, red chile beef, guajillo beef stew, mexican beef bowls, budget meal prep, mexican recipes
steps: Toast and soak the dried guajillo, ancho, and arbol chiles.
Blend the chiles with onion, garlic, oregano, and cumin, then strain the sauce.
Dredge the cubed chuck roast in flour and brown it in olive oil in batches.
Add the chile sauce, beef broth, and bay leaves and simmer 2 to 2.5 hours.
Cook the rice and portion beef, sauce, and rice into 14 containers.
